## Release candidate scope

v2.0.0-rc.4 is a security hardening and release stability prerelease for
evaluation, not a stable production baseline. It follows v2.0.0-rc.3, adds no
new product features and retains the current support policy: one Controller,
one database and one dedicated Relay, without HA. PostgreSQL 18.x and MySQL
8.4 LTS remain the supported database engines. The `v1` line is end of life and
receives no further security backports. See the
[support policy](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/reference/support-policy.md)
and [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/SECURITY.md).

### Security hardening since RC.3

- Authorization and isolation (#498): the Agent rollout list requires
  workspace-level `operation.read`; queue metrics are limited to the authorized
  workspace on PostgreSQL and MySQL; development routes require the development
  principal and a local Host.
- transportd (#498) treats an Agent result or privd receipt naming a command
  other than the dispatched one as a protocol error and publishes `Unknown` for
  reconciliation instead of success.
- Login and OIDC (#499): logins rejected only for concurrency no longer spend
  source or global rate budgets. Successful OIDC Discovery is cached for
  15 minutes with coalesced refreshes and an independent timeout; failures are
  not cached and signing keys are still refetched on rotation. Token, nonce,
  state and PKCE validation remain fail-closed.
- HTTP (#498, #500): every `/api/` response defaults to
  `Cache-Control: no-store`; JSON bodies that repeat an object member name are
  rejected; break-glass requests without a token return `400`.
- Dependency update: `filippo.io/edwards25519` v1.1.1 (#498).
- Edge image (#505): `libx11` is upgraded for CVE-2026-88806, which the
  release image scan reported on both architectures.

### Release validation

- Release Check (#503, #504) now runs Integrated Business Smoke with the four
  single-instance recoveries, Quick Install, and the release package and
  Controller image build, scan and smoke natively on both Ubuntu 24.04 amd64
  and ARM64 for the same candidate commit. A failure, cancellation, skip or
  missing result on either architecture blocks the candidate.

### Breaking changes and upgrade notes

- HTTP status changes (#500): an over-limit JSON body returns `413`; creating a
  role binding returns `409` for an existing binding or unusable approval and
  `503` when binding state cannot be read or written; a failed role or resource
  lookup during route authorization returns `503` instead of `403`. Clients that
  matched the previous `400`/`403` codes must be updated.
- PostgreSQL TLS (#498): in production, a PostgreSQL URL without
  `OCSERV_DATABASE_TLS_CA_FILE` must target loopback only, or the bundled
  `postgres` service declared by `OCSERV_DATABASE_BUNDLED_POSTGRES=true` (set by
  the shipped `compose.postgres.yaml`). Every host and fallback host in the URL
  is checked. External PostgreSQL requires a verified CA with
  `sslmode=verify-full`.
- Startup (#501): a Controller whose HTTP address is not loopback fails to
  start unless `OCSERV_ENVIRONMENT` is set explicitly. Shipped Compose files and
  scripts already set it; custom launchers must do the same.
- The database contract is unchanged from RC.3: epoch 2 (PostgreSQL revision 0,
  MySQL revision 1), with `v1.2.0@169102557cd610847c9f6ac2083336cdcf82c483`
  (epoch 1 / revision 0) as the only supported prior checkpoint. Upgrades are
  forward-only; keep a verified backup and existing audit keys. See the
  [database migration contract](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/development/control-plane.md#current-sql-artifacts-and-bounded-upgrades).

### Security and known limitations

- HTTP `503` with title `Revocation committed` still means database revocation
  committed while transport synchronization remains uncertain; there is no
  guaranteed automatic recovery interval. Do not blindly replay, bypass fences
  or edit convergence records. Follow
  [incident recovery](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/operations/incident-recovery.md#revocation-committed-with-synchronization-pending).
- An external Signer must listen on a private address and accept only the
  Controller host; see the
  [Signer runtime contract](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/development/certificates-and-signer.md#runtime-contract).
- OIDC identities are created on first login even without role bindings and
  cannot be deleted through the API; restrict sign-in at the IdP. See
  [authentication](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/operations/authentication.md).
- Release Check Business Smoke covers Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 and ARM64. The
  Extended Business profile (OIDC, certificate issue and revocation, CRL
  enforcement, Agent rollout) is a manual diagnostic outside the Release Check
  gate. Debian 13 amd64/ARM64 has bounded native package/runtime/adapter
  evidence only; Debian systemd/Controller E2E remains unverified. Hosted
  Cross-VM Enrollment does not certify Cross-VM Production. See the
  [validation scope](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/docs/development/release-checks.md).
- Native RC lifecycle checks relabel the current source under synthetic version
  identities. They do not prove upgrades from published RC.3 binaries or
  arbitrary historical releases.
- The three exact `mysql_backup` image-scan exemptions keep their 2026-10-26
  review date, installed versions and pinned MySQL 8.4.11 base digest. They
  cover reviewed Oracle Linux FIPS-channel mismatches only; new fixable
  High/Critical findings still block publication. See the
  [exemption records](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.4/deploy/production/image-scan-exemptions.json).
